label: Person
name: Abraham Than
summary:
Abraham Than (1875–1939) was a Burmese Catholic bishop who served as the Vicar Apostolic of Toungoo in Burma (Myanmar), making him one of the first indigenous Burmese Catholics to be appointed to episcopal office. His ordination as a bishop was part of the broader Catholicism's programme of creating indigenous hierarchies in mission territories — a policy associated with Pope Pius XI's 1926 encyclical Rerum Ecclesiae.

Than served in a predominantly Karen Christian community in the Toungoo region of Burma. The Karen people of Burma had converted to Christianity — both Baptist and Catholic — in significant numbers during the nineteenth century, and the Catholic Karen community in Toungoo had deep roots established by the Paris Foreign Missions Society. As an indigenous bishop leading a Karen Catholic community, Than represented a significant step in the development of a genuinely Burmese Catholicism.

His tenure as vicar apostolic came during the final decades of British Burma, before Japanese occupation in 1942 and Burmese independence in 1948. His ministry navigated the tensions between colonial Church structures and the aspirations of indigenous Catholic communities, modelling a form of episcopal leadership that anticipated the post-colonial indigenisation of Asian Catholicism that would accelerate dramatically after World War II.
